records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed CHI 2026 conference paper; arXiv version 2601.12181v2 also available
records.decision_reason: The study conducts researcher-led thematic analysis, validates a human codebook, and evaluates then deploys an LLM for corpus-scale coding, directly addressing human-LLM qualitative coding validity.

Research objective.value: Explain motivations, identity and communication strategies, and emotional outcomes in Character.AI use through Identity Negotiation Theory.
Research objective.anchor: RQ4. What are the emotional outcomes

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke, with LLM-assisted corpus annotation.
Claimed qualitative methodology.anchor: We followed the procedures of thematic analysis

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Three researchers independently screen and open-code 400 sampled Reddit posts, reach consensus, construct bottom-up themes within four theory-defined dimensions, validate the codebook on 200 new posts, iteratively tune a GPT-4o-mini prompt against the development set, and annotate all 22,374 posts.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: deductive Identity Negotiation Theory dimensions with inductive codes and subthemes

Domain.value: online discussion of Character.AI companions, identity negotiation, and emotional outcomes

Number of participants.value: not applicable to public-post corpus; three researcher-coders

Sensitive-data status.value: public social-media data containing sensitive emotional and identity disclosures; quotations were paraphrased or masked for privacy

Prompting strategy.value: Codebook-grounded chain-of-thought prompt, iteratively revised by comparison with annotations and reasoning on the 400-post development sample; final prompt disclosed in the paper/supplement.

Human role.value: Three researchers define dimensions/codes, develop themes, resolve disagreements, validate a new 200-post sample, adjudicate model annotations, and interpret findings.

Unit of analysis.value: Reddit post (title plus filtered body; replies also treated as posts)

Generated outputs.value: dimension annotations, codebook, corpus-level frequencies, themes/subthemes, and an Identity Negotiation Theory process model

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Representative source quotations and a disclosed codebook connect themes to posts, but corpus-scale LLM labels are not released as an auditable source-to-label ledger in the article.

Number of runs or seeds.value: one reported full-corpus annotation run; no repeated-run stability analysis
Number of runs or seeds.anchor: full dataset of 22,374 posts was subsequently

Automatic metrics.value: Krippendorff's alpha using a Jaccard distance/metric for multilabel annotations

Human-evaluation design.value: Three researchers independently code 200 unseen posts for inter-researcher reliability; human-model agreement is then measured on the 400-post prompt-development set after majority adjudication.

Principal results.value: Inter-researcher alpha was .73 motivation, .60 identity, .69 communication, and .69 emotion. Researcher-LLM alpha was .64, .73, .76, and .49 respectively; the resulting framework describes motivation, communication and identity strategies, and emotional outcomes.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Model selected partly for speed and cost effectiveness, but time/token/cost totals are not reported.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Institutional exemption for public data; personally identifying quotations were removed, modified, or masked; the discussion addresses emotional-data privacy risks.

Author-reported limitations.value: Single platform/subreddit may not generalize; LLM-assisted analysis may contain model bias; authors recommend cross-platform and multi-model tests.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the human-model agreement sample was the same 400-post set used to iteratively tune the prompt, so .64-.76 agreement is development-set evidence rather than a held-out test; emotion agreement remained .49 and one full-corpus run leaves instability unmeasured.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Strong evidence for a held-out, construct-level human-LLM benchmark and stability audit; it demonstrates that aggregate theme plausibility can coexist with sharply uneven dimension reliability.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed American Journal of Audiology article, published online in 2026
records.decision_reason: The study builds a human qualitative reference codebook and directly benchmarks three current LLMs for multilabel thematic coding of the complete corpus.

Research objective.value: Characterize cochlear-implant Reddit experiences and compare human versus LLM categorization accuracy and efficiency.
Research objective.anchor: comparing human and large language model

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Reflexive thematic analysis with open coding and consensus.

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Six clinically knowledgeable researchers build an inductive codebook from two 20-post rounds, pair-code and reconcile the remaining 956 posts, collapse 24 codes into five themes, and use the consensus labels to benchmark three zero-shot LLMs given the same codebook and standardized prompt.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Six researchers independently coded an initial set

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: inductive human codebook development followed by deductive LLM application

Number of documents.value: 996 Reddit posts from 22 October 2024 to 8 June 2025

Number of participants.value: not applicable to public posts; six researcher-coders

Sensitive-data status.value: public health-related social-media text; usernames/metadata excluded from model inputs and quotations adjusted for anonymity

Model family.value: OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude

Exact model/version.value: OpenAI o3, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4

Prompting strategy.value: Identical standardized zero-shot prompt and human codebook for every model; no few-shot examples or temperature adjustment; prompt supplied in Supplemental Material S3.

Human role.value: Six researchers familiar with cochlear-implant care construct and apply the codebook, resolve discrepancies by consensus, define themes, and serve as the reference standard.
Human role.anchor: research team had a background in otolaryngology

Unit of analysis.value: complete Reddit post title and body; multilabel codes
Unit of analysis.anchor: text content of each Reddit post

Generated outputs.value: 24 codes, five themes, representative quotations, and model-assigned multilabel codes

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Theme/code dictionary and representative quotations in article/supplement; no model rationale or source-span trace is reported.

Number of runs or seeds.value: one run per model; no stochastic-replication analysis reported

Automatic metrics.value: Cohen's kappa, percent agreement, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV versus final human consensus

Human-evaluation design.value: Six researchers independently code two development rounds, then three pairs independently code disjoint subsets and resolve disagreements; human Krippendorff alpha is .97.
Human-evaluation design.anchor: alpha coefficient across human annotators was 0.97

Principal results.value: Human coding produced 24 codes/five themes. Versus consensus, o3 had kappa .35, 84.8% agreement and 46.7% sensitivity; Gemini 2.5 Pro .34, 86.3% and 38.0%; Claude Sonnet 4 .25, 80.3% and PPV 30.9%. Models generally underlabelled.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Human annotation consumed 51.9 total person-hours; each LLM completed coding in less than 20 minutes; monetary/token costs not reported.
Efficiency or cost results.anchor: total time spent across all annotators was 51.9 hr

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Authors state the public, anonymous dataset involved no human subjects or identifiable information; they discuss situated ethics and make data available on request.

Author-reported limitations.value: Seven-month recent-post sample, active posters and English only, codebook/prompt constraints, uncertain human ground-truth errors, slang/typos, and no fine-tuning.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the complete corpus was not independently double-coded by all six researchers, consensus remains a fallible comparator, and single deterministic-looking outputs cannot establish stability across model service revisions.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: A useful multilabel benchmark showing that very high human agreement does not imply adequate zero-shot LLM agreement and that speed gains must be reported alongside sensitivity/precision trade-offs.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed NLP4DH 2026 conference paper in the ACL Anthology
records.decision_reason: The paper presents and quantitatively evaluates an LLM-assisted, human-steerable qualitative document-clustering system intended for Digital Humanities analysis.

Research objective.value: Develop a steerable interactive document-clustering extension that lets Digital Humanities researchers define analytical lenses and refine clusters.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: human-in-the-loop qualitative document analysis and interactive topic discovery

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Gemma 3 rewrites documents as summaries/keyphrases; instruction-tuned multilingual-e5 embeddings, UMAP and HDBSCAN produce a map; users edit clusters and can fine-tune SetFit/LoRA embeddings from few labelled examples. Component performance is evaluated with KNN label accuracy on nine benchmark tasks/datasets.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid exploratory clustering steered by researcher-supplied instructions and labels

Domain.value: Digital Humanities document exploration across reviews, lyrics, news, books, and social-media corpora

Number of documents.value: nine benchmark datasets; disclosed samples include 2,500 Amazon reviews, 5,000 lyrics, 3,600 newsgroup posts, 1,300 news summaries, 1,200 blurbs, 10,000 Reddit comments, and 8,500 news articles, plus appendix datasets

Language.value: multilingual, including English and German benchmark material

Model family.value: Google Gemma, E5, SetFit/LoRA, UMAP, and HDBSCAN

Exact model/version.value: Gemma 3 27B-instruct and multilingual-e5-large-instruct (500M), run locally; SetFit with LoRA fine-tuning

Prompting strategy.value: Straightforward user-defined rewriting prompts generate summaries/keyphrases; separate short embedding instructions define the aspect; prompts are in the appendix.

Human role.value: Envisioned users define lenses, inspect document maps, add/remove/merge/split clusters, reassign documents, and provide few-shot labels; no real-user evaluation is reported.

Unit of analysis.value: whole document represented by rewritten text and a two-dimensional embedding

Generated outputs.value: interactive document map, HDBSCAN clusters, keywords/names/descriptions/representative documents, tagged datasets

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: System displays representative documents and cluster representations, but the evaluation does not test qualitative claim-to-source traceability.

Number of runs or seeds.value: few-shot experiments repeated 10 times with different sampled training sets; other LLM rewrite stability not reported

Automatic metrics.value: KNN accuracy on the two-dimensional embedding coordinates

Human-evaluation design.value: none; workflow is illustrated with an idealized user rather than evaluated with DH researchers

Principal results.value: Instruction embeddings outperform uninstructed embeddings in 8/9 datasets; rewritten text helps 6/9; few-shot fine-tuning yields generally minor gains.
Principal results.anchor: outperform those without in 8 out of 9

Efficiency or cost results.value: Runs on a single A100 for experiments; user-facing resource/cost and latency results are not reported.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Authors motivate local open-licensed models as privacy-preserving for sensitive research data; benchmark governance/ethics analysis is not otherwise reported.

Author-reported limitations.value: The paper notes KNN accuracy is a proxy on 2D embeddings and does not evaluate HDBSCAN clustering directly; user evaluation and qualitative validity are not reported.
Author-reported limitations.anchor: does not account for the HDBSCAN

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: known-label KNN accuracy measures geometric separability, not whether a scholar's emerging themes are meaningful, reflexive, complete, or auditable; the idealized workflow supplies no usability evidence.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Useful system baseline for steerable exploration, but ARR evaluation should add real qualitative users, cluster-to-source audit, interpretive plurality, and construct-valid outcome measures.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed Social Science Computer Review article, 2026; author manuscript also available on arXiv
records.decision_reason: This is a systematic methodological review and prompt-engineering framework, not a primary qualitative-coding evaluation, so it informs methods but is not a core empirical record.

Research objective.value: Review prompt-engineering practice in LLM-assisted inductive thematic analysis and propose a four-step process for more rigorous prompting.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: systematic literature review of LLM-assisted inductive thematic analysis

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Searches Scopus, ACM, IEEE and arXiv in January-February 2025, deduplicates 130 records to 108, applies binary selection criteria, extracts six questions, and synthesizes 12 studies.

Domain.value: prompt engineering for inductive thematic analysis across health, education, transport, organizations and customer research

Model family.value: reviewed studies include GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, Llama 2, Mistral, and Gemini
Model family.anchor: Most studies utilized a single LLM

Human role.value: review authors select/extract studies and formulate prompt-engineering recommendations

Generated outputs.value: taxonomy of prompt elements/refinement practices and a four-step prompt-engineering process

Principal results.value: The 12 studies used single/multi-prompt decomposition, exemplars, role/context framing, structured outputs, iteration and ensembles; reproducibility and loss of interpretive depth were prominent limitations.

Author-reported limitations.value: Review searches ended February 2025 and its narrow LLM/thematic-analysis query and 12-study base limit completeness and currency.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: primary-study reports of high thematic alignment are heterogeneous and often based on subjective similarity; the review does not create new full-text-grounded performance evidence.
Additional validity concerns.anchor: Similarity was determined through manual inspection

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Context for preregistering prompt components, iterative refinement, response structure and reproducibility checks.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed CHI 2026 conference paper; author manuscript available on arXiv
records.decision_reason: The study evaluates an on-device open-source LLM qualitative-coding tool with qualitative researchers performing manual and assisted open coding.

Research objective.value: Understand qualitative researchers' experience, trust, privacy perceptions and methodological concerns when using an on-device open-source LLM for open coding.
Research objective.anchor: reported findings from a user study

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: mixed-method comparative user study plus deductive thematic analysis of interviews and interaction logs

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Four researchers (two novice, two experienced) manually open-code a five-page interview transcript, then use ChatQDA on the same material for one hour; researchers collect think-aloud/session logs, Likert surveys and 40-minute interviews, then coauthor-refine deductive themes.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: open coding for the user task; deductive thematic analysis of evaluation data

Domain.value: general qualitative interview coding and human-computer interaction

Number of documents.value: one five-page semistructured interview transcript used by every participant; four evaluation interview transcripts plus interaction logs

Number of participants.value: 4 qualitative researchers: 2 novice and 2 with at least two years' experience

Language.value: English study instruments/interviews; source-transcript language not explicitly reported

Sensitive-data status.value: study uses an interview transcript and argues for on-device privacy; sensitivity of the task transcript is not reported

Model family.value: OpenAI open-weight gpt-oss through Hugging Face Chat UI

Exact model/version.value: gpt-oss-20b, 20.9B MoE, MXFP4, 12.8 GiB checkpoint, 3.61B active parameters per pass

Prompting strategy.value: Chat-based iterative prompts; uploaded document and full chat history are dynamically embedded; participants freely modify prompts.

Human role.value: Researchers remain coders and reviewers, manually baseline-code, prompt and assess model outputs, and explain trust/quality judgments.

Unit of analysis.value: participant-selected excerpts and first-order codes from a five-page transcript

Generated outputs.value: excerpts, first-order codes/labels, chat reasoning, and user-study themes/design recommendations

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Current tool provides chat explanations, but participants explicitly request source spans/line references, saved settings, lockable codebooks and audit trails.

Number of runs or seeds.value: one assisted session per participant; no controlled repeated model runs

Automatic metrics.value: descriptive Likert summaries only; no output-quality benchmark against human codes

Human-evaluation design.value: Within-participant manual-then-assisted task, post-task multi-item survey, think-aloud/logs and semistructured interview; no counterbalancing.

Principal results.value: Participants valued speed (mean 3.75) but overall usefulness and trust were about 3; they reported surface-level extraction around 50-60% by perception, hallucination/inconsistency, prompt sensitivity and weakness on latent/contextual meaning.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Perceived speed mean 3.75; no objective time/cost comparison beyond the fixed one-hour session.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Informed consent and on-device deployment; surveys directly measure perceived security/privacy and authors recommend visible local-only controls, deletion, checksums and provenance.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors acknowledge the four-person exploratory sample and call for broader validation; user judgments reflect a short exposure to one transcript/system.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: manual-first fixed order, repeated use of the same transcript, n=4 and subjective accuracy estimates prevent causal or general performance claims; output quality was never independently scored.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Direct design evidence for visible privacy, source traceability, saved prompts/settings, locked codebooks and evaluation beyond perceived speed.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: CRAN software package manual for quallmer version 0.4.0, published 6 May 2026; not a peer-reviewed study
records.decision_reason: This is software documentation rather than an empirical study, but it supplies directly relevant provenance, replication, comparison and validation infrastructure.

Research objective.value: Provide an R workflow for codebook-based LLM qualitative coding, replication, reliability, gold-standard validation, segmentation and provenance.
Research objective.anchor: Qualitative Analysis with Large Language Models

Actual operationalized methodology.value: R functions create codebooks, send texts/images to provider models, convert human coding, replicate runs, calculate agreement or gold-standard validation, segment/unitize text, and inspect run ancestry/metadata.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: primarily deductive codebook application; user-defined workflows may iterate

Model family.value: provider-agnostic: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure and local Ollama models through ellmer

Exact model/version.value: not fixed by the package; version 0.4.0 records provider/model and environment metadata

Prompting strategy.value: Codebook object supplies task instructions and levels; provider parameters pass through ellmer.

Human role.value: Researchers define codebooks, select models/settings, compare replications, import human/gold coding and interpret validation.

Unit of analysis.value: named text/image item or segmented character-level text

Generated outputs.value: coded objects, reliability/comparison tables, validation metrics, segmented corpora, metadata and audit trails

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: qlm_trail plus parent-run links and captured call, model/provider, timestamp, ellmer/quallmer/R versions; named IDs can link outputs to source units.

Number of runs or seeds.value: arbitrary systematic replications via qlm_replicate; no empirical package-validation run count

Automatic metrics.value: agreement statistics including Krippendorff alpha and Fleiss kappa plus gold-standard validation

Human-evaluation design.value: none reported; documentation examples can import human or expert gold labels

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: local Ollama is supported, but the manual does not itself evaluate governance, consent or leakage.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: availability of agreement/provenance functions is not evidence that users apply them correctly or that model coding is valid; provider defaults can change unless explicitly pinned.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: A strong reproducibility implementation reference for run ancestry, exact environment capture, human-gold import, replication and unitization-aware agreement.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing 2026 proceedings paper
records.decision_reason: The study combines LLM-assisted inductive taxonomy construction with expert adjudication and a physician-validated retrieval-augmented coding/evaluation pipeline.

Research objective.value: Create a clinically grounded error taxonomy and test whether retrieved local precedents improve an LLM guardrail's coding of errors in AI-drafted portal replies.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: inductive coding and expert adjudication for error taxonomy construction

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Physician/researcher seed taxonomy is expanded by o3-mini over 1,000 stratified message triplets and refined by a board-certified physician plus 100 manually coded examples; DSPy then detects/classifies errors on 1,570 evaluation messages with or without up to five retrieved clinician precedents, against 100 physician-labelled cases.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Construction of a Clinical Error Taxonomy

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: inductive taxonomy expansion followed by deductive hierarchical multilabel error coding

Domain.value: clinical patient-portal messages and AI-drafted clinician replies across 11 specialties

Number of documents.value: 246,588 raw threads; 146,681 unique triplets/220,739 messages; 1,000 taxonomy-development messages; 1,570 evaluation messages; 100 physician-validation messages

Number of participants.value: one board-certified physician is explicitly reported for taxonomy refinement, retrieval review and 100-message reference coding; seed group size not reported

Sensitive-data status.value: de-identified EHR patient/clinician messages with pseudonymized thread IDs; retrieved local archives remain institutionally sensitive

Model family.value: OpenAI reasoning model, DSPy LLM agents, and SentenceTransformers

Exact model/version.value: OpenAI o3-mini for taxonomy induction; all-mpnet-base-v2 for 768-dimensional retrieval; exact LLM used by the DSPy guardrail is not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Looped taxonomy-expansion prompt; two-stage DSPy error detection then taxonomy classification with structured JSON/confidence/justification; enhanced condition supplies up to five similar historical pairs.

Human role.value: Clinicians/researchers seed taxonomy; a board-certified physician resolves codes, refines taxonomy, judges retrieval utility/rankings and supplies the validation reference.

Unit of analysis.value: patient query, AI draft and clinician-edited reply triplet; hierarchical domain/subdomain/error-code labels

Generated outputs.value: five-domain/24-subdomain/59-code ontology, retrieved exemplars, error-presence judgment, structured hierarchical error codes, confidence and explanation

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Pseudonymized IDs and retrieved clinician-reply precedents ground judgments; structured explanations are produced, but source-to-error trace auditing is not evaluated.

Number of runs or seeds.value: one reported pipeline condition per message; no repeated LLM stability trials

Automatic metrics.value: retrieval mean usefulness/Kendall tau; concordance, McNemar tests, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, accuracy and F1 at domain/subdomain/code levels

Human-evaluation design.value: Board-certified physician rates five retrieved examples for 56 queries and independently labels all errors in a case-control-like 100-message subset (half guardrail-positive, half negative).
Human-evaluation design.anchor: independent physician review on a 100-message subset

Principal results.value: Taxonomy grew from 6/27/37 to 5/24/59. Retrieval usefulness was .86 and Kendall tau .77. Enhanced versus baseline error-code concordance was 50% versus 33%, and F1 .500 versus .256; domain F1 .618 versus .515.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Framework is described as scalable/low-latency, but measured latency, token and cost results are not reported.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: EHR text was de-identified/pseudonymized and extraneous metadata removed to reduce privacy exposure; IRB/consent and data-sharing details are not reported in the inspected text.

Author-reported limitations.value: Only 1,000 taxonomy cases leave rare-code sparsity; generic embeddings and whole-message retrieval may miss nuanced multi-issue content; local workflow knowledge remains a blind spot.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: a single physician and 100 enriched validation cases limit generalizability and do not establish inter-physician reliability; the exact guardrail LLM is unreported, and institutional precedents can encode local practice errors.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Important evidence for retrieval-grounded coding, hierarchical validation and rare-error analysis, while underscoring the need for multiple independent experts and exact model/version reporting.
Relevance to the proposed ARR project.anchor: workflow violations were a notable blind spot

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed Learning at Scale 2026 conference paper; arXiv 2604.23255v1
records.decision_reason: The study benchmarks a locally deployed LLM for codebook-based qualitative dialogue coding across prompts/batches against researcher labels, including reproducibility, latency and energy.

Research objective.value: Quantify trade-offs among prompt design, batch size, coding performance, processing time and energy for healthcare-simulation dialogue coding.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: LLM-based deductive qualitative coding of team dialogue

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Researchers apply a pre-existing six-construct communication codebook to simulation utterances, use consensus-checked human labels as ground truth, and evaluate four few-shot prompts across eight batch sizes with a local DeepSeek-R1 14B model.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.anchor: definitions of the six communication codes

Domain.value: healthcare simulation teamwork dialogue and collaborative learning

Number of documents.value: 11,647 segmented utterances from 35 teams/sessions; 4,057 code-bearing utterances used in the LLM evaluation

Number of participants.value: 35 teams of four students (nominal 140 team-members; paper notes 15 teams in 2021 and 25 in 2022 despite reporting 35 total, an internal count inconsistency)

Exact model/version.value: Ollama deepseek-r1:14b, local; Whisper-large for automatic transcription

Prompting strategy.value: Four few-shot variants: definitions plus three examples/code; plus rules; plus rules and three preceding utterances/confidence rule; plus rules and speaker metadata. Batch sizes 1,10,20,30,40,50,60,70.

Human role.value: Two researchers double-code 20% of 2021 utterances (kappa above .7 per code); one researcher codes the remainder; human labels define the benchmark.

Unit of analysis.value: sentence-level utterance with zero or more of six communication codes

Generated outputs.value: seven binary output values per utterance, performance/time/energy tables, and Pareto-optimal configurations

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Code definitions/examples and OSF prompt/batching details are linked; outputs are compared at utterance level, but source-to-explanation traces are not produced.
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: Prompt and batching details can be found

Number of runs or seeds.value: temperature 0 and seed 42; every batch-20 configuration was run five times and produced identical outputs

Automatic metrics.value: macro F1, precision, recall, accuracy, processing time, CPU/GPU/DRAM joules, Spearman correlation and multiobjective Pareto analysis

Human-evaluation design.value: Reference-code reliability on 756 utterances from three 2021 sessions; no blinded expert qualitative assessment of LLM disagreements.

Principal results.value: Performance generally fell as batches increased; smaller batches maximized F1 while P3 around batch 20 provided a practical balance. Processing time and energy were nearly proportional (Spearman .99945), and handover remained difficult.

Efficiency or cost results.value: All 32 configurations took about 54 h 41 min on RTX A5500/dual Xeon hardware; larger batches sharply reduced time and energy; monetary cost and CO2e not estimated.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Students consented, data were locally collected/inferred, and local deployment is motivated by privacy; exact ethics-board details are not reported in the inspected text.

Author-reported limitations.value: Only four prompt designs and one batching strategy/model/corpus; long prompts may be inefficient; alternative decomposed prompts remain untested.
Author-reported limitations.anchor: alternative batching approaches were not explored

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: this is fixed-code classification rather than inductive theme construction, only part of the reference corpus was double-coded, five identical temperature-zero runs test implementation determinism more than stochastic robustness, and joules are an incomplete environmental-impact proxy.
Additional validity concerns.anchor: energy consumption directly as a proxy

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: A strong efficiency-performance benchmark design: report prompt/batch Pareto fronts, local hardware and energy while separating deterministic repeatability from model/version robustness.
